query: In conventional alloys, loss of toughness has long been associated with grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation. By contrast, compositionally complex high-entropy alloys can suppress rapid grain coarsening and deleterious intermetallic formation and have shown favorable strength–ductility combinations and resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement. These findings do not establish what governs possible toughness degradation in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy. Under the constraint of retaining a compositionally complex alloy suitable for demanding engineering service, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why brittle behavior emerges? Specify a controlled comparison that would distinguish the hypothesis from conventional-alloy expectations, predicted observations relative to the initial baseline, its service and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification outcome.

generation.hypothesis: In an initially single-phase equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA), exposure to elevated temperatures in the presence of residual oxygen causes oxygen to segregate to grain boundaries, reducing their cohesive strength and promoting intergranular brittle fracture—leading to a marked loss of fracture toughness compared with inert-aged HEA and contrary to conventional-alloy expectations where clean boundaries remain ductile under similar conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA, homogenized and annealed to a single-phase FCC structure with equiaxed grains (~50 µm) and bulk dissolved oxygen <100 ppm.
generation.intervention: Thermal aging at 600 °C for 500 h in low-pressure O₂ (10⁻³ atm) versus identical aging under high-purity argon (<1 ppm O₂).
generation.conditions: Quasi-static mode-I fracture toughness tests (loading rate 1×10⁻³ s⁻¹) at 300 K and 77 K; aging exposures explored from 400 to 800 °C for up to 1000 h.
generation.structural_mediator: Grain-boundary oxygen concentration (at.% O) measured by atom-probe tomography and TEM-EELS.
generation.mechanism: O segregation at grain boundaries lowers cohesive strength, shifting fracture from transgranular ductile tearing to intergranular brittle cracking.
generation.predicted_outcome: O₂-aged specimens will exhibit a ~30–50% reduction in K_IC relative to both as-annealed and Ar-aged baselines; Ar-aged specimens remain within ±5% of baseline toughness.
generation.boundary: Applicable for thermal exposures of 400–800 °C up to 1000 h; quasi-static strain rates (<10⁻² s⁻¹); test temperatures between 77 K and 300 K.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate uncertainty in the quantitative extent of embrittlement due to unknown oxygen segregation kinetics in HEAs.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two sets of CoCrFeMnNi specimens: age one in 10⁻³ atm O₂ at 600 °C for 500 h, age the other under Ar. Characterize grain-boundary O and measure fracture toughness.
measurements: fractography to identify intergranular vs. transgranular crack paths
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If O₂-aged specimens show ≤5% reduction in K_IC relative to Ar-aged despite grain-boundary O ≥0.5 at.%, the hypothesis is falsified.
